text:
carmen: Heads-up - customer on Dedicated reported their service endpoint (svc.prod.tenant.internal) intermittently returns NXDOMAIN from app hosts in two AZs. Happens only for in-VPC calls; public calls are fine. they say it started after a hosted-zone change earlier today.

rahul: Can you paste the minimal repro and any dig output?

carmen: Repro steps from customer (copied):
- from app host: `dig +short svc.prod.tenant.internal @169.254.169.253` -> (empty)
- `dig +short svc.prod.tenant.internal` -> NXDOMAIN
- `nslookup svc.prod.tenant.internal` -> "** server can't find svc.prod.tenant.internal: NXDOMAIN"
They also tried `curl --resolve "svc.prod.tenant.internal:443:10.2.5.12" https://svc.prod.tenant.internal/health` which hits backend but app can't resolve dynamically.

molly: That smells like split-horizon or Route53 private hosted zone overlap. Did they recently attach a new private hosted zone or move VPC associations?

carmen: Customer says they updated a developer-owned hosted zone earlier today to add a wildcard record. They attached to a different VPC but we suspect a mis-associated change.

rahul: Checklist I want run (quick):
1) `aws route53 list-hosted-zones --query 'HostedZones[?Name==`'svc.prod.tenant.internal.'`]'` (check duplicate hz)
2) `aws ec2 describe-vpcs --vpc-ids <vpc>` then `aws route53 get-hosted-zone` for each hosted zone id
3) Check resolver rule associations: `aws route53resolver list-associations`

network-oncall: Also check NodeLocal DNS cache on the app nodes. If node-local cache holds a stale NXDOMAIN it can persist even after route53 changes. `kubectl exec -n kube-system node-local-ds-xxxxx -- pkill -HUP nodelocaldns` or restart the DaemonSet.

carmen: I already got a few outputs from customer (sanitized):
```
$ dig svc.prod.tenant.internal @127.0.0.53 +noall +answer
;; -> no answer
\n$ aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=VPCId,Values=vpc-03a4f
[{
  "Id": "rra-0a1b2c3d4e",
  "ResourceId": "rslvr-1234abcd",
  "Name": "forward-to-onprem",
  "VPCId": "vpc-03a4f",
  "ResolverRuleId": "rslvr-1234abcd",
  "Status": "COMPLETE"
}]
```

rahul: Important: forwarding rules can cause NXDOMAIN if there's a precedence conflict between a VPC's private hosted zone and a resolver rule that forwards queries for the same name to an on-prem DNS that returns NXDOMAIN. Does the customer have a conditional forward for `prod.tenant.internal`?

pat: Also confirm the VPC vs hosted zone association order. If two hosted zones with overlapping names exist, the one associated with the VPC wins; if the wrong hosted zone got associated by mistake you'll see these symptoms.

carmen: I asked them to run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name prod.tenant.internal` and they returned two hosted zones: one private (hz-111) and another private (hz-222) — both private. hz-222 is supposed to be dev-only but shows association to vpc-03a4f (prod).

molly: Bingo. That explains it. Dev zone took precedence and has no record for svc.prod.tenant.internal -> NXDOMAIN.

network-oncall: Remediation options:
- detach hz-222 from prod VPC (if safe), or
- add CNAME/A record in hz-222 to forward to the real service record, or
- associate the correct prod hosted zone to the VPC and ensure hz-111 has precedence.

carmen: Customer requested we do the detach. They want to avoid downtime; we recommended a canary approach: add the record to hz-222 pointing at service IPs for a few minutes, then detach.

rahul: Also validate DNS TTLs and NodeLocal caches after change. Steps we gave: 
1) add temp record to hz-222: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id hz-222 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"svc.prod.tenant.internal","Type":"A","TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.2.5.12"}]}}]}'`
2) run `dig svc.prod.tenant.internal @169.254.169.253 +short` from app host -> should return 10.2.5.12
3) clear node-local cache `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/node-local-dns`

infra-bot: Deployment bot: route53-change/hz-222-upsert-temp-record triggered by carmen at 2024-11-05T14:02:03Z :white_check_mark:

carmen: After upsert customer reports immediate resolution in one AZ, but still NXDOMAIN from a second AZ. They said `dig` from a host in AZ-B showed NXDOMAIN until they restarted kube-dns.

network-oncall: That aligns with node-local cache isolation per AZ. NodeLocal caches run per node; some nodes keep the old NX state until flush. Restarting DNS pods should fix.

molly: Quick follow-up: we should check the TLS cert SANs too. If the app had pinned the public name but internal resolves to internal-only name, TLS handshake could fail even after DNS is fixed. `openssl s_client -connect svc.prod.tenant.internal:443 -servername svc.prod.tenant.internal` to validate.

pat: And firewall/egress allowlist: make sure there isn't an outbound block from the resolver/subnet to the Route53 Resolver endpoints or to the forwarder IPs. We saw one case where a security team blocked 53/UDP to the forwarder IP range which caused intermittent NXDOMAIN.

carmen: Customer ran `iptables -L -n | grep 53` and confirmed no egress block. TLS check shows certificate CN=svc.prod.tenant.public and SAN includes both public and internal names - OK.

rahul: OK next steps for us:
- confirm hz-222 detach schedule (prefer quiet window)
- recommend customer add the temp upsert with TTL 30 beforehand (already done)
- after detach, flush node-local caches across AZs
- monitor 5xx rate and DNS NX counts

carmen: Customer approved detach. We coordinated with networking to detach hz-222 from vpc-03a4f at 16:00 UTC. I'll run through checklist and monitor.

molly: Thanks. Please capture runbook updates so we can prevent accidental dev-hosted-zone attach to prod in the future (tagging, IAM guardrails).

carmen: Will open a postmortem with mitigation steps (record collision detection, pre-attach validation script).

pat: Nice work. :thumbsup:

carmen: Incident resolved after detach + node-local restarts across nodes. Customer confirmed app recovery and reduced latency. Closing but keeping thread for the runbook PR. :white_check_mark:
